cases.note: A source grant and exact target acceptance are both required; the reference preserves source and revision context.
Wildcard targets and operations outside the target-side policy are denied.
Mount acceptance binds to the exact immutable grant revision and target workspace.
Source operation denial and target policy denial are distinct fail-closed outcomes.
Revision, grant, and mount identities are generated by authoritative constructors, preventing caller-selected duplicate binding IDs.
Revoked and expired source relationships deny future references and update mount lifecycle state.
The access evaluator denies an expired mount even before lifecycle synchronization is called.
Historical disclosure evidence remains immutable while new disclosure attempts fail after revoke.
ReShare is rejected at grant revision construction, so a mounted memory cannot become a third-workspace source.
The migration-0087 legacy seed remains a bridge only and cannot silently become accepted target authority.
A different source binding marks the target mount stale and cannot satisfy the exact grant revision context.

known_limitations: The kernel is in-memory; durable grant revisions, mounts, disclosure audit, and migration runtime evidence are not implemented.
Transport/retrieval/cache/index/provider/export wiring and active-run revalidation remain later gates.
This fixture is executable evidence for G4, not a trusted GOVERNANCE qualification bundle.
